title: Cost Suggestion Activation Thermostat - graduated exposure, shadow simulation, operator approvals
creator: Nora Chen
description: Implement a conservative, observable activation mechanism for Optimize's batching/caching recommendations. Rather than an all-or-nothing auto-apply, this ticket introduces a 'thermostat' that regulates exposure to recommended configs via shadow evaluation, small-sample live mixing, and an operator approval matrix. Goals: 1) Protect latency and quality SLOs while realizing cost benefits; 2) Provide clear, reversible controls and runbooks; 3) Produce telemetry that ties cost delta to request slices (route/model/customer).
acceptance_criteria: 1) New activation path is callable by Optimize suggestions service and supports (a) shadow-simulate, (b) 0.5%/1%/5%/25% live mixing increments, and (c) immediate hold/rollback triggers. 2) Telemetry emitted for every step: per-segment latency P50/P95/P99, token cost, model accuracy proxy (where available), error rate, and KV cache hit ratio. 3) Approval matrix enforced: automated roll beyond 5% requires at least one PM and one SRE sign-off; production roll to >25% requires two approvers. 4) Automated rollback executes within 2 minutes of threshold breach and documents root cause. 5) Integration tests + staged e2e smoke tests in CI pass against a simulated runtime.
implementation_notes: Core components: (A) Exposure controller service that holds an exposure budget per suggestion and implements fractional routing; (B) Shadow evaluator that replays sampled requests into the candidate config and compares outputs/latency without returning mutated responses; (C) Approval gate service that records manual approvals and enforces policy; (D) Safety monitor that computes rolling metrics and triggers rollback policies. Use existing routing layer hooks and the Optimize suggestion catalog schema. Prefer non-blocking feature flags for runtime rollout. Work items: - Add exposure budget storage keyed by suggestion id and customer id - Extend runtime routing to accept fractional weights for suggestion-aware routes - Instrument shadow path to capture KV cache hits and evictions - Add policy engine rules for automatic-hold and escalation - Provide a CLI and Console UI for manual approvals and emergency rollback.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (shadow-only): enable shadow-simulate for 1000 TPS equivalent traffic for 48h on a single low-risk customer cohort. Phase 1 (micro-mix): open live mixing at 0.5% for a subset of routes for 72h; increase to 1% if no breaches. Phase 2 (pulsed ramp): 1% -> 5% -> 25% with at least 24h hold at each stage and operator sign-off at >5%. Phase 3 (widespread): after 7 days at 25% with stable metrics, allow automatic ramp per policy with daily telemetry reviews. Each step requires automated checks to pass or the safety monitor triggers automatic rollback to last stable exposure.
test_plan: Unit tests for exposure controller and policy engine. Integration test: simulated traffic runner that verifies fractional routing and shadow capture. Canary test in staging with synthetic latency spikes to validate rollback timing. Load test to validate cost reporting pipeline. End-to-end test that runs a cheap model candidate and verifies that shadow outputs are recorded but not served. CI job will include a 'safety-failure' scenario to ensure rollback works under error conditions.
monitoring_playbook: Dashboards: Optimize-Suggestion-Exposure (per-suggestion), Suggestion-Latency-Delta, KV-Hit-Ratio-by-suggestion, Cost-Delta-by-customer. Alerts: - Latency delta P95 > 50ms for 5m -> auto-hold then page SRE - Error rate increase > 0.5% absolute -> immediate rollback and incident created - Cost regression (unexpected) -> investigate; do not auto-rollback unless coupled with SLO breach. The monitoring subsystem should attach the suggestion id and exposure % to all traces. Provide a one-click 'revert to baseline' from the Console and a 'pause suggestions' global knob for emergencies.
rollback_playbook: Immediate steps: 1) Safety monitor triggers rollback API to exposure controller (set exposure to 0%). 2) Post-rollback: capture a forensics snapshot (last 60 minutes of metrics and request traces) and open incident with tags: suggestion-id, release, rollout-stage. 3) Notify stakeholders via Slack channel #optimize-rollouts and create a PRD follow-up if root cause is configurational. 4) Schedule a postmortem within 72h if rollback was triggered in production. 5) If rollback was due to model-quality regression, mark the suggestion as 'failed' in catalog and prevent re-apply until manual review.
risks: 1) Shadow simulation may under-represent cache effects that only appear at scale; mitigate by including cache priming experiments. 2) Fractional routing complexity might introduce subtle routing bugs — add runtime invariants and canary tests. 3) Approval latency could block time-sensitive cost wins — provide emergency auto-skip only for low-impact suggestions with auditor logging. 4) Large numbers of concurrent suggestions could exceed exposure budget store throughput; plan sharding and TTLs.
security_considerations: Shadow evaluation must never leak modified responses to callers. Ensure audit logging for all approval actions and encryption for exposure budgets at rest. KMS-protected keys used for audit logs; scope RBAC so only approvers can change exposure beyond threshold.
notes: This approach emphasizes observability and controlled, reversible activation over aggressive cost capture. Collaboration requests: - PM: finalize approval matrix and customer risk tiers - SRE: validate rollback timings under load - Product-Analytics: define quality proxies for non-labelled models
